title: Adaptive Token Funnel with Kernel-Probing for Latency-Sensitive Phase Splitting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket prototypes and implements an 'Adaptive Token Funnel'—a prefill/decode ingress controller that dynamically throttles and groups incoming token work by combining short-term kernel probing with attention-cost heuristics.

Goal: reduce end-to-end P99 latency for latency-sensitive requests without sacrificing overall throughput and while preserving tenant fairness. The approach blends phase-splitting (micro-phases within prefill/decode), soft token leases, and online kernel probing to pick fastpaths when beneficial.
Scope: runtime-level scheduling changes (scheduler arbiter and admission filter) and light-weight telemetry hooks. No model changes. Includes experiments across hosted and Dedicated pools.
Out of scope: cross-region routing, quota billing changes, or changes to KV cache semantics beyond tagging requests for cache affinity.
problem_statement: Prefill/decode scheduler currently treats incoming work as monolithic phases which leads to long tail latency spikes when large prefill batches occupy fast kernels or starve latency-sensitive tokens.
Kernel selection is blind to short-term contention and attention cost; some kernels favor throughput but penalize small, low-latency requests.
Existing fairness mechanisms operate at tenant weight granularity but lack a short window admission policy to avoid starvation during microbursts.
proposed_solution: Introduce an Adaptive Token Funnel (ATF) that sits at the scheduler ingress and performs: (1) per-request attention-cost estimation, (2) brief kernel probing to estimate fastpath suitability, and (3) soft-lease admission to create micro-phases that can be split/merged based on backpressure.

ATF components: attention-cost estimator (lightweight heuristic using sequence length and past attention density), kernel-prober (sub-millisecond probe batch routed to candidate kernels to measure immediate latency slope), and lease manager (gives small token execution windows that can be hedged).

Admission policy: requests flagged latency-sensitive or with low attention-cost get circuit to fast kernels (if probing passes) and receive prioritized micro-phase slots. High-cost requests are optionally chunked into decoupled batches routed to throughput-optimized kernels.

Fairness: the ATF maintains per-tenant short-term credit buckets (sliding window) so micro-phase wins are bounded; tenants that consumed extra headroom get soft-deprioritization for the next N windows.
acceptance_criteria: A/B experiment shows >= 25% reduction in P99 tail latency for latency-sensitive test set while overall token throughput decrease is < 5% compared to baseline on the same hardware mix.
Per-tenant 95th percentile slowdown (relative to baseline) stays below 1.15x for tenants not marked latency-sensitive.
No regressions in correctness: model outputs unchanged; KV cache hit semantics preserved for tagged requests.
Feature toggle implemented so ATF can be enabled per pool and per-customer for rollout.
Documentation and runbook added: explanation of metrics, toggle, and mitigation steps when kernel-probe noise occurs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype, 2w): implement ATF ingress filter and a mock kernel-prober that emits latency slope metrics. Add lightweight attention estimator based on token counts and observed attention sparsity histograms.
Phase 2 (integration, 2w): wire ATF into existing scheduler arbiter; implement soft-lease manager and micro-phase creation/teardown logic. Add per-tenant sliding-window credits and enforcement hooks.
Phase 3 (canary, 1w): enable ATF behind a feature flag in a dedicated GPU pool with a small percentage of traffic. Collect metrics and compare against control using production-like load.
Phase 4 (tuning & rollback safety, 1w): refine heuristics, add exponential backoff for noisy probes, implement quick-disable circuit in control plane, and prepare runbook.
testing_plan: Unit tests for attention estimator and kernel-prober (simulate kernels with synthetic latency distributions).
Integration test: scheduler + ATF end-to-end in staging with mixed traces (short chat, long completion, embeddings).
Load test: mixed-tenancy QPS spike tests to validate fairness buckets preventing starvation.
A/B experiment in prod-sim: measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, kernel utilization, and tenant fairness charts over 24h windows.
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary: 2 Dedicated pools with <5% traffic. Monitor automated alerts for P99 uplift or throughput drop.
If stable for 48h, expand to 10% of hosted pools (region-limited) and assign an on-call engineer to observe.
Full rollout gated on meeting acceptance criteria and SRE sign-off. Feature flag ensures instant rollback.
risks_mitigations: Risk: kernel-probing adds noise and may misroute causing oscillation. Mitigation: add probe dampening, EWMA smoothing, and fallbacks to safe default kernels.
Risk: fairness enforcement may throttle heavy-paying tenants unexpectedly. Mitigation: expose per-tenant opt-out and provide telemetry on credit consumption; conservative default weights.
Risk: estimator misclassifies attention cost for uncommon model architectures. Mitigation: detect model types and skip estimator for unsupported architectures, relying on default scheduling.
metrics: kernel_fastpath_utilization: percent of work on low-latency kernels
tenant_fairness_index: 95th percentile slowdown ratio across tenants
cache_hit_rate_tagged: KV cache hit rate for ATF-tagged requests
